papers.title: On the pure part of the cohomology of character varieties
papers.abstract: We prove the purity conjecture of Hausel and Rodriguez-Villegas relating the graded dimension of the pure part of the cohomology of the twisted character variety $M^B(r,d)$ of $GL(r)$ of genus $g$ with the cohomology of a suitable quiver variety associated to the quiver $S_g$ with one vertex and $g$ loops. In particular, this provides an explicit formula for the pure part of the mixed Hodge polynomial of $M^B(r,d)$ in terms of the Kac polynomial $A_{S_g,r}(q)$. Our approach is based on the $P=W$ theorem to transfer the purity conjecture into a statement about the perverse filtration on the cohomology of th stack of Higgs bundles on a genus $g$ curve. We use the theory of BPS Lie algebras, their $\chi$-independence property (proven by Kinjo-Koseki), the recent proof of the stack version of $P=C$ due to Picovschi and Davison's analytic neighborhood theorem to reduce the conjecture to a comparison problem between (the 'pure' part) of the BPS Lie algebra asociated to the stack of Higgs bundles on a genus $g$ curve and the BPS Lie algebra of the stack of representations of the preprojective algebra of the quiver $S_g$. This last step is taken care of by a quiver analog of Markman's tautological generation theorem for the BPS Lie algebra of arbitrary quivers (this last result is also proven by Davison and Hennecart).

papers.title: $A_1^{(1)}$-Grounded partitions at levels $1$ and $2$, Part II: affine crystal structure
papers.abstract: Grounded partitions are coloured partitions with difference conditions, introduced by Dousse and Konan, that are in bijection with the paths of the Kyoto path model of Kang, Kashiwara, Misra, Miwa, Nakashima and Nakayashiki. We describe the affine crystal structure on the grounded partitions arising from the level $1$ and level $2$ perfect crystals of type $A_1^{(1)}$. At level $1$, grounded partitions are naturally identified with $2$-restricted partitions, and the affine crystal structure is given by Kleshchev's modular branching rule for symmetric groups in characteristic $2$. At level $2$, we give explicit bracketing rules which make grounded partitions into affine crystal graphs of highest weights $2\Lambda_0$, $\Lambda_0+\Lambda_1$, and $2\Lambda_1$. We prove this by constructing explicit graph isomorphisms with the asymptotic model of Ariki and Mathas, whose vertices are Kleshchev multipartitions arising from Ariki-Koike algebras. Finally, we erase the $0$-arrows, which leaves the crystal graphs of the restrictions to the Levi subalgebra, and decompose them into finite strings. This decomposition gives new $q$-series identities at levels $1$ and $2$.

papers.title: Closed formulas for the permanents of structured matrices
papers.abstract: We give finite formulas for permanents of structured matrices and prove polynomial bounds for their evaluation. Over any field, the permanent of a matrix of bounded rank-width can be computed from the matrix alone, answering a question of Lyaudet. In characteristic $p>0$, the bound is $p^{O(k)}n^{O(1)}$, where $k$ is the rank-width. In characteristic zero, a determinant formula treats Cauchy matrices with an added polynomial of fixed degrees in the row and column nodes. This includes polynomial perturbations of Hilbert matrices and dense Toeplitz and Hankel families. For ordered cuts we give a single determinant; in positive characteristic, rational diagonal sequences give a fixed rational generating function for the Toeplitz permanents. We also give formulas for cycle weights and hook immanants. For translation matrices we obtain signed determinant formulas and classify the supports for which the permanent is the coefficientwise absolute value of the determinant. Further formulas cover cyclic block matrices, residue supports, and bands bounded on one side.

papers.title: Polytopal realization of double root free subword complexes
papers.abstract: We give a convex geometric sufficient condition for a convex polytope to realize a spherical subword complex. Using this criterion, we first prove that each root independent spherical subword complex is polytopal, for any Coxeter group. Then we prove the polytopality of double root free subword complexes, for any Coxeter groups. To prove this, we construct a polytope in an auxiliary vector space whose image under a natural affine map is the usual brick polytope. In the complex Kac-Moody case, the polytope is integral, with vertices in the character lattice of the torus of unfolded galleries in a thick building. In finite Lie types, in double root free cases, these tori are precisely the corresponding braid varieties.

papers.title: Rigidity for pivotal braided r-categories of moderate growth and applications to vertex operator algebras
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be an abelian pivotal braided r-category with simple unit object $\mathbf{1}$ over any field. We present a ChatGPT-generated proof, prompted by Bin Gui, that any object $X$ in $\mathcal{C}$ of moderate growth, in the sense that $\dim\mathrm{End}(X^{\otimes n})<n!$ for some $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, is rigid. The proof crucially uses ideas from the recent proof of Etingof and Penneys that $X$ is rigid if it is also non-negligible, that is, $X\otimes Y$ contains $\mathbf{1}$ as a direct summand for some object $Y$. In the present paper, the non-negligible assumption is removed using a rigidity criterion developed previously by the author for use in non-semisimple categories. We also present a variant result (found without further AI assistance) that $X$ is also rigid if $\dim\mathrm{Hom}((DX)^{\otimes n}\otimes X^{\otimes n},\mathbf{1})<n!$ for some $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, where $D$ is the Grothendieck-Verdier duality functor of $\mathcal{C}$. Using this variant, we show that if $V$ is a simple self-contragredient vertex operator algebra such that the category $\mathcal{C}^1_V$ of $C_1$-cofinite grading-restricted generalized $V$-modules is closed under contragredient modules, then $\mathcal{C}^1_V$ is a locally finite $\mathbb{C}$-linear abelian rigid braided ribbon category. We also show that if $V$ is a simple $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$-graded self-contragredient $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra, then the category of all grading-restricted generalized $V$-modules is a (not necessarily semisimple) modular tensor category.

papers.title: Exact module categories over $\mathrm{Rep}(u_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2))$
papers.abstract: We give a complete list of indecomposable exact module categories over the finite tensor category $\mathrm{Rep}(u_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2))$ of representations of the small quantum group $u_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$, where $q$ is a root of unity of odd order. Each of them is given as the category of representations of a left comodule algebra over $u_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ explicitly presented by generators and relations.

papers.title: Equivariant Cleft Extensions and Singular Equivalences
papers.abstract: We study the equivariant lifting of cleft extensions of abelian categories and its impact on singularity categories. Specifically, we establish the framework for lifting a cleft extension to a G-equivariant cleft extension. Furthermore, we prove that a restriction functor associated to a cleft extension induces a singular equivalence if and only if its equivariant counterpart does. As a concrete application, we demonstrate that the skew group ring of a $G$-equivariant $\theta$-extension is isomorphic to a $\widehat{\theta}$-extension of the base skew group ring, allowing us to lift singular equivalences for these structures.

papers.title: Toward a Holographic Representation Theory of the Bosonic de Sitter Discrete Series
papers.abstract: We propose a program toward a holographic representation theory of the non-scalar bosonic discrete series $\Pi^\pm_{p,q}$, $p,q\in\mathbb{N}$, $1\leqslant q\leqslant p$, of the de Sitter ($\mathrm{dS}_{4}$) group $G=\mathrm{SO}_0(1,4)$. The proposal exploits two complementary realizations of the same unitary irreducible representation (UIR): a bounded-domain realization on an open ball $\mathbb{B}$ modeling the hyperbolic space $G/\mathrm{SO}(4)$, with $\partial\mathbb{B}\simeq\mathbb{S}^{3}$, and a covariant spacetime realization on $\mathrm{dS}_{4}$, with conformal boundaries $\mathscr{I}^{\pm}\simeq\mathbb{S}^{3}$, in which the physical UIR is obtained through the corresponding gauge reduction. This leads to two boundary constructions and an explicit compatibility problem, \begin{align*} \mathbb{B} \;\overset{?\mathrm{hol}}{\longleftrightarrow}\; \partial\mathbb{B}\simeq\mathbb{S}^{3} \quad\overset{?}{\simeq}\quad \mathscr{I}^{\pm}\simeq\mathbb{S}^{3} \;\overset{?\mathrm{hol}}{\longleftrightarrow}\; \mathrm{dS}_{4} \,. \end{align*} The two outer problems seek explicit intertwiners between the bulk and boundary realizations, with their invariant norms, constraints, and physical quotients properly identified. The middle problem asks how to construct and normalize a unitary intertwiner between the two boundary realizations once both have been shown to carry the same UIR. The bounded picture exposes the unitary and harmonic structure of the representation, while the spacetime picture makes its covariant and gauge-theoretic structure manifest, allowing the two constructions to constrain and illuminate one another. The established scalar family $\Pi_{p,0}$, $p\in\mathbb{N}$, with its spherical realization on $\mathbb{S}^{3}$, provides the guiding prototype. Particular attention is given to ...

papers.title: The non-stationary $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ affine Laumon function and its difference equation
papers.abstract: We present an explicit $q$-Givental type formula for the $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ non-stationary affine relativistic Toda or affine Laumon function introduced by Shiraishi. We prove the conjecture of [J. Shiraishi, Affine screening operators, affine Laumon spaces and conjectures concerning non-stationary Ruijsenaars functions. J. of Int. Systems, 4 (2019)], that this function obeys a non-stationary difference equation involving an operator $\widehat{\mathcal T}$, which represents a quiver automorphism (Dehn twist) of the quantum cluster algebra of the affine $A_{N-1}^{(1)}$ Q-system.

papers.title: On character conductors and Sylow p-subgroups
papers.abstract: Let $P\in\operatorname{Syl}_p(G)$, where $G$ is a finite group and $p$ is a prime, and let $\chi\in\operatorname{Irr}(G)$. In 2024, I. M. Isaacs and G. Navarro asked whether the degree of $\mathbb{Q}_{p^f}$ over $\mathbb{Q}_p(\chi_P)$ is always at most the $p$-part $\chi(1)_p$ of $\chi(1)$, where $p^f$ is the $p$-part of the conductor of $\chi$ and $f\geq1$. Here $\mathbb{Q}_n=\mathbb{Q}(e^{2\pi i/n})$ is the $n$th cyclotomic field, $\chi_P$ is the restriction of $\chi$ to $P$, and $\mathbb{Q}_p(\chi_P)$ is the field generated over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ by the values of $\chi_P$. We prove that this inequality holds for $p$-solvable groups.

papers.title: Representing in Low rank II: Virtual structure and Isomorphism problem
papers.abstract: We group theoretically characterise the finite groups $G$ and number fields $F$ such that all $F$-representations of reduced degree at least $2$ are so-called exceptional. If $G$ is not a $2$-group, we obtain a full classification. Secondly, we determine whether such groups are uniquely determined by their group algebra $FG$. In particular, we obtain an instance of the virtual structure problem of Kleinert and answer the rational isomorphism problem for such groups.

papers.title: Depth-0 supercuspidal L-packets of tame covers
papers.abstract: We generalize DeBacker and Reeder's construction (or rather, its refinement by Kaletha) of depth-0 supercuspidal L-packets to tame covers of unramified reductive groups defined by \'etale levels. These include, in particular, all tame covers associated to Brylinski-Deligne data. We prove that our L-packets satisfy invariance of formal degrees and an appropriate notion of stability.

papers.title: delta-Derivations of Finite-Dimensional Simple Lie Algebras with Values in Arbitrary Modules
papers.abstract: We determine the spaces of \(\delta\)-derivations of finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebras with values in arbitrary modules for \(\delta\ne0,1\). In rank at least two, these derivations vanish unless \(\delta=\frac{1}{2}\), in which case they are precisely the module homomorphisms from the adjoint module. For \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\), we characterize the derivation spaces in terms of Casimir eigenspaces and determine when they are nonzero. When the coefficient module is simple, every nonzero derivation module is simple except possibly at \(\delta=2\), where it has a simple essential socle with a finite-dimensional semisimple quotient. We describe these modules via translation functors and give explicit formulas for the derivations.

papers.title: Infinite Index Identities for Argyres-Douglas Theories and Graded Vector Space Isomorphisms for VOAs
papers.abstract: Supersymmetric indices provide stringent tests of dualities between superconformal field theories (SCFTs). We establish infinite families of Schur-index identities among four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ Argyres-Douglas (AD) theories, with the logarithms of their fugacities related linearly. These identities connect theories with markedly different physical properties without requiring infrared duality, while still implying simple relations among their central charges and flavor levels. Through the SCFT/VOA correspondence, they become character identities for the associated affine and $W$-algebras. One broad family relates $D_p(G)$ and $(A_{(h+1)(p-1)},G)$ theories, corresponding to affine and principal $W$-algebras at boundary admissible levels. At the level of the underlying state spaces, these character identities suggest that the corresponding VOAs are related by graded vector space isomorphisms, which are weaker than full VOA isomorphisms. We explicitly construct such a graded isomorphism between the VOAs associated with $(A_1,A_{4p-3})$ and $(A_1,D_{2p})$. We also show the correspondence for universal affine and principal $W$-algebras and test its compatibility with their simple quotients by matching the lowest-degree null states. We establish analogous character identities for certain non-vacuum modules in concrete examples and conjecture a broader extension. Finally, beyond the SCFT/VOA correspondence, we discover similar identities between level-one affine and Virasoro algebras, whose further generalizations point toward a new spectral level-rank duality in WZW models.

papers.title: Matrix ultraproducts have trivial fundamental group
papers.abstract: We prove that every tracial ultraproduct $\prod_{\mathcal{U}} M_n(\mathbb{C})$ of matrix algebras has trivial fundamental group. In particular, this establishes that there are uncountably many nonisomorphic matrix ultraproducts, answering a question of Sorin Popa. We actually prove the stronger result that every matrix ultraproduct has trivial first-order fundamental group and thus our techniques are model-theoretic in nature.

papers.title: Universal TT- and TQ-relations via centrally extended q-Onsager algebra
papers.abstract: Let $A_q$ be the alternating central extension of the q-Onsager algebra, a comodule algebra over the quantum loop algebra of $sl_2$. We classify one-dimensional representations of $A_q$, and show that spin-j K-operators constructed in arXiv:2301.00781 act as K-matrices previously obtained in the literature. Using these K-operators and K-matrices, we construct universal spin-j transfer matrices generating commutative subalgebras in $A_q$. Within a technical conjecture, we derive their fusion hierarchy, the so-called universal TT-relations. On spin-chain representations of $A_q$, we show how the universal transfer matrices evaluate to spin-chain transfer matrices, and as a result we get explicit TT-relations for all values of spins for auxiliary and quantum spaces, any inhomogeneities, and general integrable boundary conditions. In particular, we derive previously conjectured TT-relations. Using the TT-relations, we show that n-th local conserved quantities of the spin-j chains of length N are polynomials of total degree 4Njn in two non-local operators of the q-Onsager algebra. As a result, we give an algorithm of explicit calculation of all local conserved quantities in terms of spin operators. Furthermore, using the universal TT-relations we derive exchange relations between spin-j Hamiltonians and the two non-local operators showing non-trivial symmetries for special boundary conditions, that they commute with all Hamiltonian densities. As another application of our universal TT-relations we propose universal T-system, Y-system and universal TQ-relations for $A_q$, and as a result, universal TQ for the q-Onsager algebra. For diagonal boundary conditions, we also obtain universal TT- and TQ-relations for a degenerate version of $A_q$ known as centrally extended augmented q-Onsager algebra. We finally discuss implications of our results for generalized Gibbs ensemble construction.

papers.title: Supercuspidal, discrete, and elliptic densities for reductive groups over non-archimedean local fields
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be the group of points of a connected reductive group over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of arbitrary characteristic, with residue field of size $q$. For a principal congruence tower $K_n$ attached to a Lie algebra lattice $\mathcal{L}$, the supercuspidal and discrete series proportions of the Plancherel mass of the $K_n$-fixed vectors both converge, with error $O(q^{-n/4})$, to the probability that a Haar-random form in the dual lattice $\Lambda=\mathcal{L}^\vee$ is elliptic. For $\mathrm{GL}_d$, the supercuspidal limit confirms a prediction of Howe. This probability is positive, and we characterize when it is one. More generally, outside a union of congruence cells of total mass $O(q^{-n/4})$, each cell determines a common Levi class for the supercuspidal and discrete series supports of every tempered representation containing its character. The limiting mass of each class is the probability that a Haar-random form in $\Lambda$ lies in the corresponding stratum. The proof combines finite Fourier analysis, quantitative estimates for parabolic incidence maps, and a Jacquet-module argument that detects unitary exponents.

papers.title: Folding of cluster algebras
papers.abstract: We develop a general framework for folding cluster algebras from simply-laced Cartan data equipped with admissible finite-group actions. For arbitrary finite sequences, we establish folding of root data, compatible pairs, $\bfi$-box seeds, and their individual cluster variables, without reducedness, finite-type, or acyclicity assumptions. In the reduced case, the folding is realized through quantum unipotent coordinate algebras and is compatible with dual PBW generators. It sends cluster monomials associated with canonical lifted $\bfi$-box seeds to elements of the classical dual canonical basis for the quotient Cartan datum. For arbitrary positive braids in finite Cartan type, the folding is realized through quantum virtual Grothendieck rings and, after specialization at $q=1$, is induced by a single ambient Grothendieck-ring homomorphism. Finally, for arbitrary symmetrizable Cartan data and arbitrary positive braids, we prove that the Laurent homomorphism identifying corresponding seed variables restricts to a surjective algebra homomorphism between the corresponding cluster algebras. We also extend the Kimura--Oya quantum twist automorphisms to arbitrary positive braids after localization at the frozen variables, and prove that their commutative specializations commute with the folding homomorphisms.

papers.title: Admissible Yang--Baxter equation for Nijenhuis perm superalgebras
papers.abstract: We develop a superization of the theory of admissible Yang--Baxter equations for Nijenhuis perm algebras initiated by Ma and Song. We introduce Nijenhuis perm superalgebras, their representations, and the dual representation, with Koszul signs chosen so that the contraction of the Yang--Baxter tensor matches the $\mathcal O$-operator equation exactly. We define Nijenhuis perm superbialgebras and characterise them by matched pairs. In the coboundary case, we show that every even supersymmetric solution of the $S$-admissible perm Yang--Baxter equation gives rise to a Nijenhuis perm superbialgebra, and we give sufficient conditions for a perm superalgebra to admit a Nijenhuis operator constructed from such a solution. Examples with purely odd components illustrate the role of the grading.

papers.title: Dualizing involutions on Kazhdan-Patterson covers of $\mathrm{GL}(r)$
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic zero and $G=\mathrm{GL}(r,F).$ Let $r,n \geq 2$ and $\widetilde{G}$ be an $n$-fold Kazhdan-Patterson cover of $G$. Let $\pi$ be an irreducible smooth representation of $G$ and $\pi^{\vee}$ be the contragredient of $\pi$. Let $\tau$ be an involutive anti-automorphism of $G$ satisfying $\pi^{\tau}\simeq \pi^{\vee}$. In this case, we say that $\tau$ is a dualizing or duality involution. When $r=2$, it is known that any lift of the standard involution on $G$ to $\widetilde{G}$ is a dualizing involution if and only if $n=2$. In this paper, we study the dualizing property of the lifts of the standard involution on $G$ to $\widetilde{G}$ and prove the following: (i) When $r \geq 2$ and $n \geq 3$, we show that any lift of the standard involution to $\widetilde{G}$ is never a dualizing involution. (ii) When $r=2t$ and $n=2$, we show that any lift of the standard involution to $\widetilde{G}$ is a dualizing involution. (iii) When $r=2t+1$ and $n=2$, we show that there is a unique lift of the standard involution to $\widetilde{G}$ which is a dualizing involution.

papers.title: On non-vanishing of the first Hochschild cohomology of blocks
papers.abstract: Let $B$ be a block of a finite group algebra $kG$, where $k$ is an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$. Inspired by the result of Fleischmann, Janiszczak and Lempken that $\mathrm{HH}^1(kG) \not=0$ when $p$ divides the order of $G$, Linckelmann conjectured that $\mathrm{HH}^1(B)\not= 0$ when $B$ has non-trivial defect. By developing the methods of Briggs, Rubio y Degrassi and the author, we give a fusion theoretic criterion for non-vanishing, proving the conjecture holds for all blocks of abelian defect. Further, we show the criterion holds for all blocks at $p > 5$, proving the conjecture for all such primes

papers.title: Syzygy matrices and higher extensions over string algebras
papers.abstract: Over a finite-dimensional string algebra, higher extension dimensions may eventually vanish, become periodic, or grow without bound. We show how their behaviour can be read from a finite directed graph. Second syzygies split into uniserial modules from a finite family; their syzygies define a nonnegative integer matrix, so higher extension dimensions become weighted counts of walks. Only the part of the graph relevant to the chosen pair of modules contributes. This gives four growth regimes: eventual vanishing, periodicity, quasi-polynomial growth, and exponential growth. We derive the construction from projective covers, give explicit extension formulas over truncated cycles, and illustrate the growth regimes with examples.

papers.title: Graded unitarity constraints on simply-laced affine Kac--Moody algebras
papers.abstract: We investigate constraints imposed by four-dimensional unitarity (recently formalised as graded unitarity) on possible simply-laced affine Kac--Moody vertex algebras arising from four dimensions via the SCFT/VOA correspondence. Under the assumption that the $\mathfrak{R}$-filtration is weight-based with respect to the currents and the Casimir operators, with appropriately shifted $R$-charge assignments for the latter, we demonstrate that all values of the level other than a discrete set are incompatible with four-dimensional unitarity. This set includes all the boundary admissible affine vertex algebras, those corresponding to rank-one Kodaira SCFTs, as well as certain non-admissible families conjecturally associated with specific $D^b_q(\mathfrak{g})$ Argyres--Douglas theories. Specialising to $\mathfrak{sl}_N$ with $N$ prime, we find a stronger result: under the same $\mathfrak{R}$-filtration assumption, four-dimensional unitarity rules out all levels except the boundary admissible $k = k_{N,q}$, which are precisely those corresponding to the $D_q^N(\mathfrak{sl}_N)$ Argyres--Douglas theories.

papers.title: Exceptional model structures and the induced extriangulated categories
papers.abstract: A Hovey triple $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{F}, \mathcal{W})$ is {\it exceptional}, if $(\mathcal{C} \cap \mathcal{F}, \ \mathcal{C} \cap \mathcal{F} \cap \mathcal{W})$ is not a Frobenius pair. One has a disjoint union $\{\text{Hovey triple}\} = \{\text{Hereditary Hovey triple}\} \ \dot\bigcup \ \{\text{Exceptional Hovey triple}\}$ \ $\dot\bigcup \ \{\text{non-hereditary and non-exceptional Hovey triple}\}.$ Exceptional Hovey triples appear widely. For a selfinjective Nakayama algebra $A= kC_n/J^t$, $A\mbox{-}{\rm mod}$ admits exceptional Hovey triples if and only if $\gcd (n, t) \ge 2$ and $t \geq 3$. Their homotopy categories reveal new phenomena. Nakaoka-Palu's Theorem implies that there is a triangulation on $\frac{\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F}{\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F\cap\mathcal W}.$ It is proved that a Hovey triple in a weakly idempotent complete extriangulated category $(\mathcal A, \mathbb E, \mathfrak s)$ is exceptional if and only if the induced extriangulated structure $\bigl(\frac{\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F}{\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F\cap\mathcal W}, \ \overline{\mathbb E}, \ \overline{\mathfrak s}\bigr)$ is not {\it canonically triangulated}. Between this extriangulated structure and the one arising from the triangulation, the intermediate extriangulated structures are in one-to-one correspondence with Serre subcategories of $\mathrm{fp}((\frac{\mathcal P(\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F)}{\mathcal C\cap\mathcal F\cap\mathcal W})^{\mathrm{op}}, \mathrm{Ab})$.

papers.title: Tilting theory on continuous quivers (I) maximal rigid and tilting subcategories
papers.abstract: Let $\mathrm{rep}(\mathbb I)$ be the category of finitely generated persistence modules on the interval $\mathbb I\subseteq\mathbb R$. We study the maximal rigid subcategories of $\mathrm{rep}(\mathbb I)$. Maximal rigid interval consistent subcategories are classified via tilting modules over the corresponding discrete type $A$ quiver. We compare several related notions, (weak) tilting and maximal rigidity, in both the context of hereditary abelian categories with enough projective objects and $\mathrm{rep}(\mathbb I)$ and prove that every maximal rigid interval consistent subcategory is weak tilting and every maximal rigid consistent below subcategory is tilting. In addition, any maximal rigid subcategory $\mathbf T\subseteq \mathrm{rep}(\mathbb I)$, not necessarily being interval consistent, satisfies $\mathbf T^{\perp_1}=\mathop {Gen}(\mathbf T)$. We also establish a continuous analogue of Ingalls-Thomas's bijection by showing a bijection between integrally supported maximal rigid consistent below subcategories and integrally generated torsion classes.

papers.title: Rings with unequal $\operatorname{silp-spli}$
papers.abstract: For a unital associative ring $R$, let $\operatorname{silp}(R)$ be the supremum of the injective dimensions of all projective right $R$-modules, and let $\operatorname{spli}(R)$ be the supremum of the projective dimensions of all injective right $R$-modules. We construct an explicit non-Noetherian unital algebra \[R=k1\oplus \frac{k(0\longrightarrow1\longrightarrow2\longrightarrow\cdots)} {\langle\text{all paths of length }2\rangle}\] over any field and prove that $\operatorname{silp}(R)=1$ and $\operatorname{spli}(R)=\infty. $ The algebra is the unitization of the non-unital path algebra of the one-sided infinite ray modulo paths of length two. The example answers the question whether $\operatorname{silp=spli}$ raised by Gedrich and Gruenberg.
